newsitem.title: ITALY: Lira ERM reentry unlikely this weekend-sources.
newsitem.headline: Lira ERM reentry unlikely this weekend-sources.

text.p: Italy is unlikely to lodge a request for the lira to be readmitted to the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) this weekend even though the main body of the 1997 budget bill has been approved by the lower house of parliament, a monetary source said.
"It would be difficult for it to happen this weekend," said the source. "The time available to activate the procedure this weekend is very limited."
Government ministers have said that they would like to seek lira reentry into the ERM by the end of November once the budget has cleared the lower house.
The first step towards returning the lira to the currency grid would involve Italy requesting that a meeting be called of the EU monetary committee in Brussels.
"The only certain thing is that you have to act while markets are closed and you need a meeting of the monetary committee, followed by consultation by EU Finance Ministers," the source added.
"In theory we could even proceed next Saturday but nothing is decided, perhaps we will do it later but in any event during November," said the source.
The monetary committee has meetings scheduled for November 19 and 26 which will be devoted to discussion of European economic and monetary union.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has said the lira's current market levels would be appropriate for ERM reentry. The lira was quoted at 1,006.75/7.25 lire against the mark late on Friday. Rome newsroom +396-6782560
